# Spec: Smart Inbox Triage

## Background
Support agents spend too long sorting the shared inbox. We will add smart
triage so the important things surface first and the noise drops away.

## Goals
Make the inbox feel fast and relevant. Reduce time-to-first-response. Agents
should trust the ordering enough to work top-down.

## Proposed Behaviour
When a message lands, the triage service assigns it a priority using the
relevance engine. High-signal messages move to the top of the queue; low-signal
ones are collapsed into the digest lane. The engine considers sender standing,
message urgency and account tier.

Agents can override a placement. Overrides feed back into the engine so it
learns the team's preferences over time.

The digest lane is summarised and delivered on the usual cadence.

## Implementation Sketch
- New `triage` service subscribing to the ingest stream.
- Priority written to `messages.priority_band`.
- Inbox UI sorts by band, then by arrival.
- Overrides recorded in an events table for later training.

## Notes
- The relevance engine is the same one the recommendations team uses.
- Sender standing should probably reuse whatever reputation signal we already
  compute, if that is still running.
- We may want to expose triage to end customers eventually.
- Migration for existing unread mail: TBD.
